newsitem.title: USA: US High Court allows dismissal of smoker lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: US High Court allows dismissal of smoker lawsuit.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court let stand Tuesday the dismissal of a lawsuit on behalf of a longtime smoker against two tobacco firms and two industry groups for fraud, negligence and defective cigarette design.

The family of Samuel Allgood, a smoker who died in 1989 from throat cancer complications, sued RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co; a U.S. unit of B.A.T Industries Plc ; the Tobacco Institute Inc; and the Council for Tobacco Research-USA Inc.
The lawsuit, filed in Houston, claimed the defendants contributed to Allgood's death through fradulent misrepresentations regarding their efforts to discover smoking's health consequences.
It also charged the defendants fradulently concealed the health risks of smoking, negligently produced and marketed cigarettes and defectively designed and marketed cigarettes.
A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit in 1995. A U.S. appeals court in April upheld the decision, rejecting the family's request that a trial be ordered.

The appeals court said the negligence, conspiracy and product liability claims were barred by the two-year statute of limitations and the fradulent concealment claims were barred under a 1992 Supreme Court decision.
Alden Holford, a lawyer for Allgood's family, appealed to the Supreme Court to hear the case.
"If the court of appeals' opinion stands, then none of over 400,000 Americans who are killed yearly by tobacco use could ever find justice," he said in his appeal.

Laywers for the tobacco companies and the trade groups said the rulings in the case were largely based on Texas law and the case presents no important federal question warranting Supreme Court review.
The high court sided with the tobacco defendants, rejecting the appeal without any comment or dissent.
